import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Convert 'is_takeaway' to a more descriptive categorical label
df['is_takeaway_label'] = df['is_takeaway'].map({0: 'Dine-in', 1: 'Takeaway'})

# Aggregate total sales by product and takeaway status
sales_by_product_takeaway = df.groupby(['product', 'is_takeaway_label'])['total'].sum().reset_index()

# Sort products by their overall total sales for better readability
# First, calculate total sales per product regardless of takeaway status
total_sales_per_product = df.groupby('product')['total'].sum().sort_values(ascending=False).index
# Apply this order to the 'product' column in the aggregated dataframe
sales_by_product_takeaway['product'] = pd.Categorical(
    sales_by_product_takeaway['product'], 
    categories=total_sales_per_product, 
    ordered=True
)
# Sort the aggregated dataframe by the new categorical 'product' column
sales_by_product_takeaway = sales_by_product_takeaway.sort_values('product')

# Set aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create the figure and axes for the plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))

# Create a grouped bar chart
sns.barplot(
    data=sales_by_product_takeaway,
    x='product',
    y='total',
    hue='is_takeaway_label',
    palette='viridis' # Choose a color palette
)

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Total Sales by Product and Order Type', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Product', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=12)
plt.legend(title='Order Type', fontsize=10, title_fontsize=12, loc='upper right')
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right', fontsize=10) # Rotate x-axis labels for better readability
plt.yticks(fontsize=10)

# Improve layout to prevent labels from overlapping
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the plot
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
